subject: FinWise - Performance SLO & customer-led load test coordination
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@finwise.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs + customer-led load test (FinWise)

Alex — thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we're all aligned before your customer-led run: 

Summary of SLOs you shared on the call
- Target p95 end-to-end response latency: <= 250ms for non-streaming responses
- For streaming (progressive token delivery) we expect initial token within 120ms and p95 full-response completion <= 400ms
- Sustained throughput target: 200 requests/sec during peak window
- Concurrency: up to 50 concurrent sessions during the peak window

What Redwood will provide
- A pre-provisioned test API key and test account (separate from prod)
- k6 script (we'll share a starter script you can run/modify) and a Locust alternative if you prefer
- IP ranges to allowlist (we'll provide a CSV)
- A short monitoring checklist: token-level breakdown, per-route latency, and error-rate expectations

Customer asks / open items
- You wanted to run the load test from your infra (customer-led) — we'll provide all artifacts and confirm exact endpoints
- Confirm a 2-hour test window and a preferred day/time — you mentioned next week as possible (please confirm below)

Attachments I'll share in follow-up: k6-finwise-loadtest-v1.js (starter), allowlist-ips.csv, finwise-test-accounts.csv

Next steps (action owners)
- Rishi (SE): will post the k6/Locust script plus instructions and expected failure thresholds
- Aditya (Perf Eng): will confirm any special kernel/quantization model variants to use for the test and expected baseline numbers
- Alex / FinWise: confirm test window (date + start/end in your TZ) and provide IPs that will run the test
- Marissa: will coordinate and create the HubSpot log and Slack channel for real-time updates

Success criteria proposal (please confirm):
- Error rate < 1% across test window
- p95 latency within the targets above
- No sustained CRC/connection failures from your side or ours

Thanks — will follow up shortly with the scripts and allowlist.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123
From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@finwise.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: FinWise Ops <ops@finwise.com>, Michael Chen <michael.chen@finwise.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T17:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs + customer-led load test (FinWise)

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. That matches what we discussed. A few quick items from our side: 

1) Preferred test window: Aug 10, 2026, 10:00–12:00 PDT (we can shift 1 hour earlier/later if needed)
2) We'll run the tests from two GCP regions (us-west1 and us-east1); I'll attach the source IP ranges from our load generators after internal approval
3) Agree with the success criteria — want to add: no more than 5% increase in 99th percentile latency vs our light baseline run (we'll share baseline numbers)

Couple of clarifying Qs: 
- Will the test use streaming endpoints or non-streaming? We'll likely test both; if you can confirm the endpoint names for each that helps.
- How will we receive the test API key? (secure share or Vault?)

I'll attach a quick list of IPs and the contact who will run the scripts.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Garcia
SRE Lead, FinWise
alex.garcia@finwise.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@finwise.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs + customer-led load test (FinWise)

Alex / Marissa — adding technical detail and the starter k6 script. Attaching: k6-finwise-loadtest-v1.js (starter) and allowlist-ips.csv (Redwood egress ranges). High-level notes: 

Test endpoints (pre-prod/test namespace):
- Non-streaming: https://api-test.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
- Streaming: https://stream-test.redwood-inference.com/v1/stream

k6 notes (starter script):
- Default scenario ramps to 200 RPS over 10 minutes, holds for 60 minutes, then ramps down.
- We include a streaming scenario that opens SSE/WebSocket connections and measures time-to-first-token and full-response completion.
- Authentication: use Authorization: Bearer <TEST_API_KEY>. We will provide the test key via secure share (1Password/secret link) once we have the final list of runner IPs.

Failure thresholds we recommend embedding in the script (these will abort the run if breached):
- global http_req_failed rate > 1% for more than 5 minutes
- p95 latency (non-streaming) > 300ms for more than 3 minutes (treat as fail for this run)

Observability / telemetry we will push during the run:
- Per-request latency histograms (p50/p95/p99)
- Error types (4xx vs 5xx vs connection errors)
- Throughput per minute, concurrency over time

IP allowlist / network
- Attached is allowlist-ips.csv (Redwood egress). Please add these to your firewall for the test window so callbacks/streams are allowed.

Attachments: k6-finwise-loadtest-v1.js (starter), allowlist-ips.csv

I'll post the k6 script link in Slack as well and be online during your window.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@finwise.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: FinWise Ops <ops@finwise.com>, Michael Chen <michael.chen@finwise.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs + customer-led load test (FinWise)

Rishi — got the script and allowlist, thanks. A couple of items from our infra team: 

- We've confirmed test window Aug 10 10:00–12:00 PDT.
- Test runners will come from these IPs (attached in this reply): 34.72.120.12, 34.72.120.13 (us-west1), 35.190.10.45 (us-east1).
- We'll need the test API key sent to our Vault admin: vault-redwood@finwise.com. Please send via secure link.
- Streaming validation: can you confirm how we should assert "initial token within 120ms"? We typically measure time-to-first-byte on the connection, but streaming token boundaries can vary. Any recommended asserts in the script?

Also attaching finwise-test-accounts.csv with the test accounts you'll provision.

—
Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@finwise.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs + customer-led load test (FinWise)

Alex — perfect, thanks for confirming the window and IPs. Quick confirmations and a couple of housekeeping items before the run: 

1) Test API key delivery: Rishi will generate a scoped test key and send a 1Password secure share to vault-redwood@finwise.com 24 hours before the run.
2) Streaming asserts: Rishi, suggested approach is to record time-to-first-token (TTFT) at the client and assert TTFT <= 120ms for p95. For full-response completion we assert p95 <= 400ms. Please confirm these are implemented in the k6 streaming scenario.
3) Success criteria (finalized):
   - Error rate (all 4xx/5xx) < 1% over the 2-hour window
   - p95 non-streaming <= 250ms, p95 streaming full-response <= 400ms
   - No more than 5% regression on p99 vs FinWise baseline for the window (per Alex's ask)

I'll create the HubSpot activity and a Slack channel (#finwise-loadtest) and add everyone. We'll have real-time monitoring in the Redwood Console: latency dashboards and tracing hooks.

Next steps (short list):
- Rishi: confirm TTFT assertion in the k6 script and send the 1Password link (to vault-redwood@finwise.com)
- Aditya: please post any notes about model variants/quantization we should pin for this run (if none, say so)
- Alex: we'll expect the final IP allowlist by EOD Aug 7 so we can validate firewall rules on our side

Thanks everyone — excited to get this validated.

—
Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@finwise.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs + customer-led load test (FinWise)

Alex / Marissa — quick final check from my side: 

- Confirmed: k6 streaming scenario includes TTFT measurement and will assert p95(TTFT) <= 120ms. Full-response p95 assertion set to <= 400ms.
- I'll generate the scoped test API key and send a 1Password secure share to vault-redwood@finwise.com tomorrow (Aug 9).
- No special model variants required for this run — we will use the standard xlarge quantized runtime (Aditya: confirm if you'd like a different variant).
- I'll be online during the entire window and we'll post live metrics to the Slack channel. If error rate exceeds 1% for more than 5 continuous minutes, we'll pause and triage.

Attachments in this thread: k6-finwise-loadtest-v1.js, allowlist-ips.csv, finwise-test-accounts.csv

See you during the run.

—
Rishi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
